description:
FILED s449q (Opus round-7 agent Q), from the #621 probes.  PRE-EXISTING and
NOT dup-specific -- it is the general `open` re-open rule, which is why it is
its own task rather than a #621 residue.

REPRODUCER:

    open(my $k, '<', "/etc/hostname") or die;
    my $r = open($k, '<', "/no/such/file/xyz");    # fails
    printf "ret=%s fileno=%s\n", (defined $r ? $r : "undef"),
           (defined(fileno($k)) ? fileno($k) : "undef");
    my $l = <$k>;
    print "read-after=[", (defined $l ? $l : "undef"), "]\n";

        perl  ret=undef fileno=undef read-after=[undef]
        PCL   ret=undef fileno=5     read-after=[bernpad\n]   <-- the OLD file

CAUSE: perl's do_open closes the handle's existing IO *before* it tries the
new open, so a failed open leaves the handle CLOSED.  PCL's %p-open-impl only
calls %p-install-fh when a stream came back, so on failure the previous stream
is still bound to the handle and still readable -- SILENT WRONG: the program
reads the OLD file thinking the new one is open.

Also visible through the dup path: `open($keep, "<&NOSUCH")` (which is now a
plain undef return, task #621) leaves $keep's fd in place where perl reports
fileno undef.

WHERE: `%p-open-impl` in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp -- close+forget the handle's
existing stream before the open is attempted (NOT after it fails: perl closes
first, so even a SUCCESSFUL re-open must not leak the old descriptor -- probe
that half too).  %p-close-impl / %p-forget-fh are the mirror pair to reuse.

BAR before fixing: probe vs perl (a) failed re-open of a lexical handle,
(b) failed re-open of a BAREWORD handle, (c) successful re-open (the old fd
must be gone -- compare fileno numbers), (d) re-open of STDOUT (the #535
descriptor rule must still hold), (e) an in-memory handle re-opened onto a
file, (f) a re-open whose SOURCE is the handle itself (`open($k,"<&",$k)`).
Guard rows in Pl/t/fileio-02.t.
subject: A FAILED open on an already-open handle leaves the old handle open and readable; perl closes it first, so the handle is closed
